E1.evidence: Issue #67 gives the reproducer (launch usb_cam with pixel_format="mjpeg" instead of "yuyv") and the log line "[swscaler @ 0x1545460]  deprecated pixel format used, make sure you did set range correctly"; several later commenters reproduce it (Kinetic/16.04, Melodic/18.04). The maintainer-merged PR #115 names the same warning.

E2.evidence: usb_cam (ROS 1 driver node) links the FFmpeg libraries: it decodes MJPEG with libavcodec and passes the decoder's avcodec_context_->pix_fmt into libswscale's sws_getContext (src/usb_cam.cpp at f80cff39, line 448: "video_sws_ = sws_getContext(xsize, ysize, avcodec_context_->pix_fmt, xsize, ysize, PIX_FMT_RGB24, SWS_BILINEAR, NULL,"). libswscale treats the full-range YUVJ pixel formats as deprecated and warns when one is passed (libswscale/utils.c, e.g. tag n2.8 line 1134: "av_log(c, AV_LOG_WARNING, "deprecated pixel format used, make sure you did set range correctly\n");"). The warning depends on the pixel-format value crossing the usb_cam/FFmpeg API boundary, so it is not internal to either unit; the resolving change is in usb_cam code (not launch/config, not build).

E3.evidence: PAIR: usb_cam feeds the pixel format obtained from the decoder into the scaler API of FFmpeg on every MJPEG frame; the warning is observed while the two run together ("If launching the same node with pixel_format ="mjpeg"  the terminal outputs a continuing stream of these warnings").

E4.evidence: Observed warning stream in the issue body; reporter states the image otherwise works ("But the frames seem to be captured normally otherwhise, and the live image works fine.").

units.name: usb_cam
units.revision_basis: The reporter (2017-04-25) first used the master branch and then says "the same warning appears also for the code from the dev branch". The develop branch head on 2017-04-25 was f80cff39 (Merge pull request #58, committed 2017-01-26); master head on that date was 3f0e0587 (0.3.4, 2015-08-18), which also shows the warning. The fix for ROS 1 is PR #115 merged into develop on 2022-10-25 with merge commit 37451954, which descends from f80cff39 (18 commits ahead). The ROS 2 backport PR #189 (branch ros2, merge 4ab2952d) is the PR the issue was closed against but does not apply to the ROS 1 branch the reporter used.

units.name: FFmpeg
units.revision_basis: The reporter does not name an OS, distro, or FFmpeg/libav version; the only version hint is a later commenter's guess ("I think Ubuntu updated their ffmpeg libraries"). Later reproducers name Ubuntu 16.04 + Kinetic and Ubuntu 18.04 + Melodic binaries but not library versions. The warning string is present in libswscale/utils.c (e.g. at tag n2.8). The resolution does not change FFmpeg, so the resolved revision equals the (unknown) broken revision.

failed_conditions.quote: [swscaler @ 0x1545460]  deprecated pixel format used, make sure you did set range correctly

loudness_evidence: The provider library itself prints the diagnostic: "the terminal outputs a continuing stream of these warnings: `[swscaler @ 0x1545460]  deprecated pixel format used, make sure you did set range correctly`" (https://github.com/ros-drivers/usb_cam/issues/67). It is emitted when a scaler context is initialised; usb_cam creates a new context per frame (sws_getContext ... sws_freeContext inside mjpeg2rgb), so it recurs during running rather than once at activation.

resolution.summary: usb_cam lowers the FFmpeg log level at MJPEG decoder initialisation (av_log_set_level(AV_LOG_ERROR) in UsbCam::init_mjpeg_decoder), suppressing the libswscale warning; the pixel format passed to sws_getContext is not changed.
resolution.evidence: PR #115 (merged into develop 2022-10-25, merge commit 37451954) adds "av_log_set_level(AV_LOG_ERROR);" with the comment "// Suppress warnings of the following form:" and its description says "This warning can be safely ignored at present. Long term libjpeg-turbo could be used instead of libav to decode mjpeg frames." (https://github.com/ros-drivers/usb_cam/pull/115). The issue was closed with "Closed as fixed in favour of #189" (the ROS 2 backport). No source shows the resolved composition running with an identified FFmpeg revision.

notes: Eligibility is a judgement call: the offending pixel-format value is produced by FFmpeg's own MJPEG decoder (libavcodec) and consumed by FFmpeg's scaler (libswscale), with usb_cam passing it through unchanged; I treat FFmpeg (libavcodec, libswscale, libavutil, released together from one repository) as one provider unit and the defect as usb_cam's use of the API with a full-range YUVJ format that libswscale expects to be expressed as a normal YUV format plus a separate range setting (libswscale/utils.c handle_jpeg maps AV_PIX_FMT_YUVJ422P to AV_PIX_FMT_YUV422P before the warning). If FFmpeg's decoder/scaler pair is judged to be the real composition, the case would be internal to FFmpeg. Canonical form: the C struct member is written as field:libavcodec/AVCodecContext.pix_fmt (library name in the pkg slot) because no form for C struct members exists. Inventory is capped at 10; usb_cam also uses avcodec_register_all, av_frame_alloc, avpicture_alloc, av_init_packet and avpicture_layout. api:av_log_set_level is used only in the resolved composition. UPGRADE is possible but not documented: a commenter only guesses "I think Ubuntu updated their ffmpeg libraries", and no provider revisions are named. The packet's fix_ref rt-net/sciurus17_ros#118 is a downstream project that avoided usb_cam altogether (replaced uvc_camera with libuvc_camera) and cites this warning as the reason for not adopting usb_cam; it is not a fix of this composition. The ROS 2 backport PR #189 (ros2 branch, merge 4ab2952d) applies the same change to the ROS 2 driver.
